title: Element rotated by a quarter turn in one orientation only
user_impact: Users with fixed-mount screens (e.g. wheelchair-mounted) see the content sideways and cannot turn the device to read it.
technical_impact: rotate or a rotating transform under @media (orientation) differs by 90 degrees from the value in the other orientation.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.4 Orientation; Media Queries 4 (orientation); CSS Transforms 1 and 2 (transform, rotate); ACT b33eff
checks.applicability: Rendered elements that a style rule under @media (orientation: landscape|portrait) gives the rotate property or a transform with rotate(), rotateZ(), rotate3d(), matrix() or matrix3d().
checks.expectation:
Fails when the element's rotation about the Z axis in landscape differs from
the one in portrait by a quarter turn (90 degrees modulo 180): the element
turns back when the device turns and stays in place, so only one orientation
shows it upright. Compared is the value that applies in each orientation
(!important first, then the style attribute, then the last matching rule),
including a rotation without a media query as the base (2.5deg, and 92.5deg
in landscape, fails). A full turn, 45 degrees or the same quarter turn in
both orientations passes. A rotation without an orientation media query
applies in both and is not applicable, as are translations only, an invalid
orientation value (the query is false) and inline styles set by script.
Further media conditions next to the orientation, a selector this check does
not decide or a value it cannot evaluate (var()) give a review, not a
violation. Elements not rendered (display: none) are out of scope. Whether an
orientation is essential is a human judgement. Reported once per element.
